lines.say: Angle chasing is like a treasure hunt. Each angle you find is a clue to the next.
Every step uses one rule, and you write the reason in brackets.
Straight line, 180. Around a point, 360. Vertically opposite angles are equal.
With parallel lines, F and Z angles are equal. C angles add to 180.
lines.write: F, Z equal;  C adds to 180

lines.say: Angles in a triangle add to 180.
Tick marks show equal sides. Equal sides mean equal base angles.
lines.alt: Isosceles triangle with apex 40 degrees and base angles 70 degrees

lines.say: If the apex is 40 degrees, each base angle is 180 minus 40, halved. That's 70.
The equal angles sit opposite the equal sides. Not next to the apex.
Extend one side of a triangle. The angle outside is an exterior angle.
lines.alt: Triangle with side extended; exterior angle equals a plus b

lines.say: It equals the two inside angles that aren't next to it.
Both the straight line and the triangle make 180. Remove the shared angle and a plus b is left.
A B equals A C, and the apex is 52 degrees. B C is extended to D.

draw.alt: Isosceles triangle ABC with apex 52 degrees, BC extended to D

lines.say: Step 1. The base angles are equal. 180 minus 52 is 128. Half is 64.
Step 2. Straight line at C. 180 minus 64 is 116.

draw.alt: Exterior angle ACD of 116 degrees found

lines.say: Check with the shortcut. 52 plus 64 is 116. It matches.
Sometimes no rule links the angles. Then draw your own extra line.
A line bends at E between two parallel lines. 41 degrees at A, 33 at C.
lines.alt: Parallel lines with a bent line through E

lines.say: Draw a dashed line through E, parallel to both. Now you see two Z shapes.
lines.alt: Dashed parallel line through the bend splits it into p and q

lines.say: The top part is 41, the bottom part is 33. Alternate angles.
Bent line equals add. So angle A E C is 74 degrees.
Angle A is x, angle B is 2x. The exterior angle at C is 132.
lines.alt: Triangle with angles x and 2x and exterior angle 132 degrees

lines.say: 3x equals 132, so x equals 44.
So angle A is 44 and angle B is 88. Angle A C B is 180 minus 132, which is 48.
Check. 44 plus 88 plus 48 is 180.
Only use F, Z or C if the lines are marked parallel.
Don't add the exterior angle into the triangle's 180.
Reread the question. Don't stop at x if it asks for an angle.
Clue to clue. Write every angle on the diagram.
Bent line between parallels equals add.
Outside equals the other two inside.
Ticks talk. Equal sides mean equal opposite angles.
